title: UK Government and UKRI Unveil £78M ($103.8M USD) Quantum Commercialization, Networking, and Skills Package - Quantum Computing Report
gist: The UK government and UKRI announced a £78M quantum package: £50M in sensing/PNT innovation grants, £20M for quantum-networking supply-chain components, and an £8M expansion of the QuEST apprentices programme. EPSRC added a separate £17M call to integrate quantum computing with AI and HPC. The package is weighted toward near-term, dual-use sensing and PNT, in support of a 2030 goal of global leadership in quantum sensing.

insights.claim: The UK's £78M quantum package, delivered through UKRI's Quantum Technologies Priority Programme, splits into £50M for commercial sensing and positioning grants, £20M for quantum-networking supply-chain components and £8M to expand the QuEST Apprentices Programme.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
entities: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
insights.so_what: UK public money is going mainly to sensing and PNT, the segment closest to revenue, more than to computing hardware.
insights.locator: Delivered through UKRI’s Quantum Technologies Priority Programme

insights.claim: The funding directly supports the UK's goal of global leadership in quantum sensing by 2030, within the broader £2 billion, 10-year National Quantum Strategy.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: UK quantum sensing companies have policy tailwinds and a likely government customer base through 2030.

insights.claim: The EPSRC Quantum Technologies Theme has an average annual baseline budget of £33 million and focuses on moving quantum physics out of academic labs into dual-use civilian, NHS and national-security infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A dual-use framing points to defence and NHS procurement as the first commercial channels for UK quantum firms.
insights.locator: Ahead of the UK National Quantum Technologies Showcase

insights.claim: Beneficiaries of the £50M sensing/PNT competition include MoniRail (train positioning and track-fault monitoring where GPS is unavailable), Siloton (handheld OCT eye scanners for NHS screening), ColdQuanta UK (compact quantum radio antennas for defense PNT) and Cerca Magnetics (wearable OPM-MEG brain scanners for epilepsy).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This names the UK quantum-sensing companies with government-validated use cases, candidates for later private rounds or acquisitions.

insights.claim: Other sensing beneficiaries include QLM Technology (greenhouse-gas quantum cameras for utility infrastructure) and Quantum Fabrix (satellite quantum clocks for defense and telecoms).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Methane detection and resilient timing are clear revenue applications for quantum sensing.

insights.claim: The prominence of GPS-denied positioning, defense PNT and satellite clocks in the awards shows the UK treating quantum PNT as a resilience hedge against GNSS disruption.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defense-driven demand for alternatives to GNSS is a durable driver of quantum-sensing procurement.

themes.theme: Networking supply chain, skills and hybrid compute

insights.claim: The £20M commercial networking stream, involving Aegiq of Sheffield and component suppliers, targets a domestic supply chain for photonic chips, single-photon sources, specialized lasers and quantum communication nodes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sovereign supply-chain funding for components signals a push to onshore critical quantum hardware inputs.

insights.claim: The £8M QuEST expansion, run through Harwell Incubator and QuEST North, aims to train 150 specialist quantum and engineering technicians by 2030.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A shortage of technicians, not just PhDs, is a constraint on scaling, and 150 people by 2030 is small relative to industry needs.

insights.claim: Separately, EPSRC opened a £17M call, closing in December 2026, with awards of up to £3.75M to integrate quantum computing with classical HPC and AI workflows, covering hybrid orchestration software and AI-driven error mitigation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Policymakers treat quantum as an accelerator inside HPC/AI stacks, which benefits hybrid orchestration software vendors.
